label: COUNTS-ONLY amendment v2 (2026-10-31): tensor-contraction IC (ic.tensor_contraction_v1, m = 2) against rho.negation and the prime IC baseline on the registered bench-roster prime curves of 16 bits (counted S only, no wall time)
description: Supersedes, for counted S only, docs/ecbench/specs/tensor-ic-vs-rho-16.json (left frozen and unchanged; measurement there: rounds 1, warmup 1, order alternate_measured, L2, timeout_seconds 1800). Same curves, targets (target_seed 20261030, 8 per curve), arms, arm methods, measurement seed 20261030. Only measurement changes. Gate-forced change: isolation_required L2 to L0. On EKS the run-ecbench L2 gate grades any solve under 1 ms as L1 (record.rs MIN_SOLVE_WALL_NS_V3) and exits 42, and rho at 10-16 bits solves in microseconds (run gh-41008826427-1: 176/192 records L1); L0 is the level ecbench documents as sufficient for operation counts. Discretionary changes, filed before any data (protocol v2): warmup 1 to 0 (a warm-up only absorbs one-time wall costs, which counted S does not see; with warmup 0 the measured round uses absolute seed index 0, which the original's single measured round, index 1, did not use). Rounds (1), order (alternate_measured) and timeout (1800 s) are the original's. timeout_seconds is a wall-clock limit (runner.rs): at L0 whether a row ends verified or timeout depends on the host; a timeout row is host censoring (unknown), never a negative result. No wall-time figure from this session is a result. Caveat: on 64-bit builds lambda <= 64, root_u = lambda/131072 = 0 and public inputs take the finite-size fallback; nothing here exercises the recursive subexponential kernel; ic.tensor_contraction_v1 is an exponential toy (protocol H1). Protocol: research/hashed_ecdl_counts_20261031/protocol.json (v2).
